_comment: Spymaster registry config (docs/iteration-architecture.md step 2, codenames/spymasters/registry.py). Each entry names a Spymaster subclass (see SPYMASTER_CLASSES) and its constructor params. 'trained' marks whether this entry expects a trained artifact (a checkpoint) before it can be built -- false for every baseline here, since none of them train. The 'learned' entry has no checkpoint_path in its params (there is no single fixed checkpoint -- it comes from whichever training run a caller wants); scripts that need it call registry.spymaster_spec('learned', checkpoint_path=..., ...) to merge in the real path at call time rather than building this entry directly. 'roles' says which scripts pick an entry up without naming it: 'baseline' is the standard comparison set (both arenas), 'exploration' is an upper-bound tool that only scripts/pipeline/run_two_team_arena.py offers, 'trained' needs a checkpoint supplied per invocation. A new entry omitting 'roles' defaults to ['baseline'], so it appears in the arenas automatically.
